title: Station jobs (the long poll's answer)
description: The hub's 200 answer to GET /api/station/jobs?wait=<seconds> (Hub._jobs, Jobs.take, sizeup/cloud/hub.py): the work the hub has for the station, read by StationLink._jobs (sizeup/cloud/station.py). The request has no body. `wait` is how long the hub holds the request while it has nothing: a decimal number of seconds, cut to 0..30; missing or not a number is 0. The station always asks wait=25 with a 40 s timeout and asks again as soon as it has an answer. Every open job is in one answer, oldest first, and is handed out once only (J1); `jobs` is empty when the wait ran out or the hub is deploying. The station runs each job on a thread of its own and posts the outcome to POST /api/station/jobs/<id> (station-job-result). It reads `jobs`, and of a job `id`, `type` and `args`.

jobs.description: The jobs to run now; [] for none.

id.description: 16 lower-case hex characters, made by the hub for this job. The outcome goes to POST /api/station/jobs/<id>, a route that takes no other form of id.

type.description: The kind of job. A station answers one it does not know with ok false and `this station doesn't know job '<type>'`.

args.description: The job's arguments, by `type`: the three objects below (their type is said here, once).

type.description: A function of the station's App to run.
A reset of an incident source.

tts.description: `tts`: say a dispatch with the station's voice, for a hub without one (Cad._render_remote, sizeup/cad/service.py). The hub waits 20 s. Outcome: `label` and `audio` (station-job-result).

text.description: The dispatch as text. Empty after trimming, no string, or over 4000 characters: `no dispatch text`.

tones.description: The tones before the voice: groups in order, each a list of [hz, seconds] pairs; [] for none.

prefixItems.description: Its frequency, Hz.
Its length, seconds.

repeat.description: How often the message is said; the station cuts it to 1..3 and takes 2 for a missing one or 0.

additionalProperties.description: How the unit is said; "" for as written.

spoken.description: Per unit code, how it is said aloud. Anything but an object is taken as {}.

voice.description: The voice the hub is set to.

engine.description: The speech engine; the station takes `kokoro` for a missing one.

voice.description: The engine's voice name; "" for its own default.

speed.description: The speaking rate as a factor, 1.0 = normal.

fallback_voice.description: The voice of the fallback engine.

rate_wpm.description: Words per minute for the fallback engine; 0 for the voice's own.

sources_reset.description: `sources_reset`: an admin on the hub resets an incident source on the station (Hub.reset_source). The hub waits 30 s. Outcome: `result`, a sentence. The station takes only an object with a string `source` ("" for every source, asked for by name) and refuses anything else (#791; before it, arguments that were no object reset every source, J5).

source.description: The source's id; "" for every source that can be reset.

by.description: Who asked, for the station's log; "" when the hub does not know.

call.description: `call`: run one function of the station's App (Hub.remote; StationLink._call). The hub waits 12 s (10 s for sources_poll_now). The hub sends the arguments by position (a list), for older stations. A station from #791 on takes them by position or by name (an object keyed by `x-names`), ignores a name it does not know and a position past the function's last parameter, and refuses a call that leaves out a required parameter (before #791 one argument too many was answered ok false with the TypeError's text, J4). `x-names` on each list below gives the parameter each position lands on, checked against the App's signatures; `x-forms` the lengths the hub sends today.

fn.description: The function. The station runs only those of CALLS (sizeup/cloud/station.py) and answers any other with ok false and `not allowed from the hub: '<fn>'`, a text the hub looks for (D2).

args.description: The arguments, by `fn`: the lists below, as the hub sends them (that they are lists is said here, once); to a station from #791 on also an object by name. Missing or null: refused (`<fn>: no args ...`); a required parameter left out: refused (`TypeError: <fn>() missing argument ...`); anything but a list or an object: `args: a list or an object` (before #791 a missing or empty one ran the function on its defaults, J5).

call.set_mode.description: App.set_mode(mode, sdr=None, by="person", confirm=False): give a dongle a job. The hub sends [mode, sdr], and [mode, sdr, "person", true] when a person confirmed taking a fire job's dongle for another system's job. Result: null when switched, else a sentence saying why not.

prefixItems.description: mode: the job, as the station's status names it: a channel's label, the county P25 job, another system's job, or Off.
sdr: the dongle's serial; null for the station's first dongle.
by: who chose it. The hub sends `person` (a person's choice is never changed by auto-assign).
confirm: true when the person confirmed the station's question.

call.set_talkgroup.description: App.set_talkgroup(tg, record=None, main=None, tier=None, system=""): a talkgroup's switches. The hub sends [tg, record, main] for the county system's, and [tg, record, main, tier, system] when a tier or another system is named, but only to a station whose status has `p25_systems` (an older one raises TypeError on five arguments). Result: null, else why not.

prefixItems.description: tg: the talkgroup's number.
record: keep its calls; null leaves it as it is.
main: on the main list and attached to our incident; null leaves it as it is.
tier: another system's talkgroup's tier; null leaves it as it is.
system: the P25 system's name; "" for the county's.

call.set_talkgroup_group.description: App.set_talkgroup_group(group, record=None, main=None): every county talkgroup of one section at once. Result: null, else why not.

prefixItems.description: group: the section's name, as the talkgroup list has it.
record: as in set_talkgroup.
main: as in set_talkgroup.

call.retranscribe.description: App.retranscribe(ids=None, as_alt=False): run speech-to-text again. The hub sends [ids], and [ids, true] for the alternative text of a channel set to both engines. [null] is every recording still on the station's disk, asked for by name; an empty or missing argument list is refused (#791; before it, every recording too, J5). Result: how many were queued (an integer).

prefixItems.description: ids: the clips; null for every recording on disk.
as_alt: true when the text is wanted as the alternative, not as the transcript.

call.set_channel_prefs.description: App.set_channel_prefs(prefs, aws=None, tones=None, squelch=None): the hub's whole map of per-channel choices. The hub sends [prefs, aws, tones], and [prefs, aws, tones, squelch] only to a station whose status has `channels.squelch_ok` (an older one raises TypeError on four arguments). Result: the station's `channels` status object, which the hub puts in place of the one it had.

prefixItems.description: prefs: per channel key (a label, `tg:<n>`, `p25:<system>:<n>`) the choices that differ from the defaults; {} for none. The station refuses the whole call for one bad entry (ValueError). `p25:` keys are left out for a station whose status has no `p25_systems`.

engine.description: Which engine reads it. Also `pin:<engine id>` (a GPU worker, `station:<id>`, `aws`): sizeup/sttroute.py. A station without `engine_select_ok` is sent only `local`, `aws` or `both`.

prefixItems.description: aws: whether the hub can take audio for Amazon Transcribe now.

why.description: When not, why, for people; the station keeps 300 characters.

reserve.description: Channels that keep Amazon Transcribe past the monthly limit; at most 40 kept.

deny.description: Channels of another system past their own budget. Sent only when there are any, and only to a station whose status has `channels.deny_ok`.

deny_why.description: Why they are denied, for people. Sent with `deny`.

prefixItems.description: tones: the tone pairs named on the hub, per `<a_hz>/<b_hz>` key; {} for none. Each value is the hub's settings entry as it is (name, a_hz, b_hz, ours, ...): not typed here.

additionalProperties.description: One named pair, as the hub's settings keep it.

prefixItems.description: squelch: per FM traffic channel label, the squelch numbers set on the hub; {} for none. What does not fit the station's channels is left out there, never refused.

open_db.description: Opens at this many dB of quieting (4 to 30).

close_db.description: Closes under this many dB (2 to 28, under open_db).

min_open_s.description: Seconds an opening must last to be kept (0.1 to 2).

call.emergency_all_clear.description: App.emergency_all_clear(tg=None, radio_ids=None): an alarm's All clear on the hub closes the emergency window on the station. Result: true when one was open there.

prefixItems.description: tg: the talkgroup the alarm was on.
radio_ids: the alarm's radio IDs.

call.transcribe_now.description: App.transcribe_now(ids): the hub's fallback when Amazon Transcribe could not read a live clip: the station's whisper at live priority. A station without it answers `not allowed` and the hub sends `retranscribe` instead (D2). Result: how many were queued.

prefixItems.description: ids: the clips.

call.catch_up.description: App.catch_up(specs): clips skipped while speech-to-text was behind, to be read once the station's whisper is idle. The hub sends at most 3 a call; the station takes the first 10. A station without it answers `not allowed` and is not asked again for 10 minutes (D2). Result: {queued, refused, hold}.

prefixItems.description: specs: one per clip, the hub's row for it as it is.

items.description: One skipped clip. The station reads id, key, source, unit, start and service (the transmission's own fields when it still has it in memory) and ignores the rest; an entry that is no object, or whose id is no clip id, is skipped without a word.

key.description: Its speech-to-text channel key: a label, `tg:<n>` or `p25:<system>:<n>`. The station keeps 60 characters.

source.description: The channel's label or the talkgroup's name. The station keeps 60 characters.

unit.description: Who talked, when known; "" otherwise. The station keeps 120 characters.

start.description: When the transmission started, Unix seconds.

seconds.description: How long it was, in seconds. Not read by the station.

service.description: The source's service (fire, police, ...); "" for none. The station keeps 16 characters.

tier.description: The talkgroup's tier; "" for none. Not read by the station.

tries.description: How often the catch-up tried it before. Not read by the station.

tried_at.description: When it was last tried, Unix seconds; 0 for never. Not read by the station.

route.description: Where the hub's catch-up sends it: always `whisper` here. Not read by the station.

call.set_adsb_receiver.description: App.set_adsb_receiver(serial): the dongle reserved for ADS-B. Result: null, else why not.

prefixItems.description: serial: the dongle's serial; "" for none. (The App also takes null; the hub sends "".)

call.set_antenna_groups.description: App.set_antenna_groups(raw, confirm=""): all of the station's antenna groups ([] for none). The hub sends [groups], and [groups, confirm] when the person confirmed the station's question. Result: null, else why not; a text starting `confirm: ` is a question to put to the person.

prefixItems.description: raw: the groups, as the person saved them. The station refuses the whole call for one that is no object, has a bad name, or whose sdrs or jobs are no lists of strings.

items.description: One antenna group. Keys it does not know are ignored.

name.description: 1 to 24 letters, digits, space . / + & _ -; unique without regard to case.

jobs.description: The jobs they are locked to, in order of rank.

prefixItems.description: confirm: the station's question, word for word, as the person confirmed it. The station refuses it if its question has changed since.

call.sources_poll_now.description: App.sources_poll_now(reason=""): a pre-alert or an airport alert on the hub: the incident-source adapters on the station poll now. Result: how many adapters were woken.

prefixItems.description: reason: what happened, for the adapters' logs (the station keeps 40 characters). `phone pre-alert` never wakes one.

call.reception_post.description: App.reception_post(body, by="", tid=""): start, stop or annotate a reception test on the station. The hub always sends all three, with by "": who asked stays on the hub. Result: null, else why not.

prefixItems.description: body: the person's request as posted to the hub. Other keys by action; start: `system`, `job` or `jobs`, `sdr`, `minutes`, `keep_min`, `pause`, `note`; note: `id`, `note`. Not typed here.

action.description: What to do. Any other word is answered with why not.

prefixItems.description: by: always "" from the hub.
tid: the id the hub made for a test being started (12 hex characters); "" otherwise.

call.reception_sample_b64.description: App.reception_sample_b64(sid): one call a reception test captured, to listen to. Result: a string, the base64 of a WAV file, "" when there is none. The hub decodes it strictly (validate=True) and takes it only if it starts with RIFF.

prefixItems.description: sid: the sample's id, from the station's reception status.

call.set_stt_alert_keys.description: App.set_stt_alert_keys(keys, rev): the sources the hub's pre-alerts push from. Sent only to a station whose status has `stt_alert_rev`, when that differs from the hub's. Result: {ok, rev}.

items.description: A source key (`fm:<label>`, `p25:<system>:<n>`); the station keeps 64 characters.

prefixItems.description: keys: the source keys, sorted. More than 500, or no list, is refused (ValueError).
rev: the revision of that set (station-state `status.stt_alert_rev`). A boolean or a float is refused.

call.set_stt_terms.description: App.set_stt_terms(payload): the top of the private term lists for whisper's prompt. Sent when the station's status `stt_terms.v` differs from the hub's. Result: {v, sets}, the station's `stt_terms` status object.

prefixItems.description: payload: every list. The station refuses the whole call (ValueError, its copy kept) for more than 8 sets, a bad name, terms or version.

v.description: The version of all lists together: 12 hex characters, "" for none.

sets.description: Per list name (lower case, digits, underscores; 32 characters at most), the list.

items.description: One term, as said on the air.

terms.description: The terms, the most useful first.

places.description: Whether the places list is added to it in a prompt; taken as true when absent.

call.quarantine_dismiss.description: App.quarantine_dismiss(kind): an admin's Dismiss on Settings > Station > Health (Hub.dismiss_rejected, POST /api/cad/health/dismiss) for the alert "Station event rejected by hub: <kind>": the station drops the events of that type the hub refused that it no longer sends again (state `stuck` or `late` in its quarantine, sizeup/cloud/outbox.py dismiss); one still being sent again stays. Result: how many went (0 on a station without a hub link).

prefixItems.description: kind: an event `type` (station-events), as the quarantine's status lists it under `kinds`. The hub sends only a word of this pattern (else 400 before any job); the station takes any string and matches it exactly.
